messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER 1: Service: inference-prod. Region: eu-central-1. Symptom: sudden 502/503 surge at ALB fronting inference pods, concentrated in AZ eu-central-1c. Error rate ~14% over last 1m. Paging @oncall-jordan and @sre-kai.

oncall-jordan: Oncall here, acknowledge. Pulling up ALB/NLB + ingress-controller dashboards.

sre-kai: Looking at ingress-controller (Contour/Envoy) metrics 1 upstream reset and tcp connection aborts from pods on nodes in eu-central-1c. Node-level dmesg shows NIC errors and soft-reset events.

netops-ana: Confirmed: AWS VPCFlow logs show elevated RST/ERR for instances in eu-central-1c and increased latency on the AZ gateway. No recent deploys. Route53 weighted records unchanged.

infra-lee: Checking node autoscaling/rolling updates. No recent kubeadm or kernel upgrades. One older kernel on nodepool-eu-c-02 though.

incident-bot: :information_source: Incident severity set to SEV-2. Notifying customer-success for impact comms.

customer-success: Were seeing incoming tickets for 502s from two customers. Drafting status note. Hold until mitigation in place.

sre-kai: Quick repro from inside VPC against pod IP returns connection reset 70% of the time: 

```
curl -sS -X POST http://10.0.34.122:8080/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -i
# sometimes returns: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\n# envoy log: "upstream reset before headers" / "connection refused"\n```

netops-ana: Opening AWS support chat, filing SR. Also recommend failing traffic away from eu-central-1c to eu-central-1a/b while we mitigate. We can temporarily set TG weights or update ALB target registration.

oncall-jordan: Plan: 1) Remove/disable targets in eu-central-1c from ALB TG (manual deregister) 2) Cordone + drain suspect nodes in eu-central-1c 3) Scale up capacity in a/b to absorb load 4) Re-route any sticky sessions to healthy AZs. Executing now.

infra-lee: Running cordon/drain:
```
kubectl -n inference cordon ip-10-0-45-123.eu-central-1.compute.internal
kubectl -n inference drain ip-10-0-45-123.eu-central-1.compute.internal --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference -o wide
```

sre-kai: Deregistering targets for eu-central-1c now (ALB):
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:123456:targetgroup/inference-tg/abcdef --targets Id=i-0cdef... --region eu-central-1
```

deploy-bot: :rocket: Autoscaler triggered: nodegroup eu-central-1a +4 nodes to compensate.

netops-ana: ALB metrics show 5xx rate dropping within 2m of removing eu-central-1c. Still watching for residual errors from client connections that were already routed.

customer-success: Sending status update to affected customers: "We detected elevated errors for inference requests in eu-central-1 beginning at 03:05 UTC. Traffic has been routed away from the affected AZ and most requests have recovered. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a post-incident summary." :white_check_mark:

sre-kai: After draining two nodes and restarting envoy on one pod, 502/503 count is down to baseline. Captured pprof and heap profiles from pods that showed frequent GC; attaching to ticket.

incident-bot: :memo: AWS SR opened: SR-888888. Support indicates a transient hardware/networking maintenance in eu-central-1c affecting host NICs during 03:00-03:20 UTC.

infra-lee: Note: there were a few pods with older kernel TCP stacks that showed higher retransmit sensitivity; we're scheduling a node image update for that nodepool.

oncall-jordan: Quick runbook additions from this event:
- Add TG fractional-unhealthy detector alarm (if >10% targets unhealthy in an AZ for 2m, auto-weight down)
- Add cross-AZ packet-loss SLO and alert (from VPCFlow/NLB metrics)
- Add staged failover playbook to avoid manual deregisters as first step

netops-ana: Also recommend enabling ALB cross-zone load balancing temporarily on next fail to reduce impact of single-AZ egress issues (we had C-ZLB off for cost reasons).

customer-success: Customers have acknowledged the update and are asking for a postmortem. We'll gather impact windows per tenant.

sre-kai: Action items captured for postmortem: collect node dmesg, NIC stats, envoy logs, pprof, TZ-synced timestamps, ALB/NLB request traces, Route53 logs. Schedule postmortem in 48h.

deploy-bot: :truck: Rolling update queued for nodepool-eu-c to bump kernel and reboot 3 nodes outside business hours.

oncall-jordan: Monitoring 5xx and latency for 30m. If stable, we'll close the active incident and convert to follow-up ticket. Thanks team. :bow:
